questions.q: According to the lesson, why does AI risk management ask a harder question than traditional IT risk management?
options: Because a system working exactly as designed can still produce an unfair or unsafe outcome at scale, with no outage to alert anyone
Because AI systems never have outages
Because traditional IT risk management doesn't consider reputational damage
Because AI systems are always more expensive to build
questions.explain: The lesson's key point is that AI risk can hide inside normal, working-as-designed operation, unlike an outage that triggers an alert.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the three kinds of AI risk described in the lesson?
options: Risk to the people affected by the system's decisions
Risk of the office Wi-Fi going down
Risk of running out of meeting room space
Risk of the marketing budget being too small
questions.explain: The three kinds are risk to the organization, risk to the people affected, and risk to the model itself.

questions.q: In the lesson's simple risk-tiering approach, what two factors are scored for a given AI system?
options: Likelihood of a bad outcome and the impact if it happens
Model file size and training time
Number of developers on the team and their job titles
The system's marketing budget and its release date
questions.explain: The lesson's tiering method scores likelihood and impact, each roughly high/medium/low.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what should a system that scores high on both likelihood and impact receive?
options: The most expensive controls: human review, bias testing, documentation, and approval gates before major changes
No additional oversight, since high-risk systems are usually well-built already
Immediate shutdown with no further evaluation
A lower priority than low-risk systems, since it's already working
questions.explain: High likelihood and high impact systems should receive the heaviest governance controls per the lesson's tiering logic.

questions.q: The lesson compares its risk-tiering logic to which earlier concept in this course?
options: The Critical Data Element criteria from Chapter 4
The Stripe subscription billing tiers
The course's video-rendering pipeline
The header navigation bar design
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says the 'spend effort where it matters' logic mirrors how Chapter 4 taught prioritizing Critical Data Elements.
